key_insight: A metallic alloy’s composition and processing recipe can be inferred in reverse from its optimized microstructure and texture, with conventional hand-crafted descriptors outperforming learned embeddings in this small dataset.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a data-driven route for alloy recipe back-calculation, helping materials engineers narrow candidate compositions and extrusion settings when designing for target properties.
method: Built a 107-sample magnesium alloy extrusion dataset spanning 14 alloys, with optical micrographs and X-ray texture measurements.
Compared three microstructure/texture representations: conventional grain and texture statistics, pretrained vision embeddings, and a graph neural network over the grain network.
Used prediction heads for two inverse-design tasks: infer alloy composition from processing conditions, and infer process parameters from composition.
evidence_signal: Under 5-fold cross-validation, conventional descriptors identified the correct alloy for 65% of held-out cases versus a 17% majority-class baseline, and they also reduced process-temperature error relative to using composition alone.
watch_item: The study is limited by a small, discrete dataset with only a few alloys and press settings, so the inverse predictions may not generalize well beyond the observed options.
paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
